one_sentence: The Grace Operator G, a non-unitary idempotent projection, structurally models prevenient grace as an external, irreversible sign-flip from fallen to redeemed.
executive_summary: This document formalizes the doctrine of prevenient grace using non-unitary operator algebra. It defines a Grace Operator G that acts on a two-state Hilbert space, mapping both |+1> and |-1> to |+1>, satisfying idempotency (G²=G) and non-unitarity (G†G≠I). This captures key theological properties: grace originates externally (cannot arise from internal dynamics), is complete in one application (idempotency), and is irreversible (singular, rank-1). The mapping connects to impossibility theorems from ISO-002, showing that closed systems cannot self-generate grace. The document acknowledges reverse-engineering risk but provides falsification conditions and independent mathematical consequences. It concludes that the isomorphism is structurally valid but is a formalization rather than an independent discovery.
short_summary: This document is a structural isomorphism record mapping the Grace Operator G from non-unitary operator algebra to the Christian doctrine of prevenient grace. The core claim is that grace acts as an external, idempotent, non-unitary projection that flips the moral sign from -1 to +1, requiring voluntary reception. Key evidence includes the mathematical properties of G (idempotency, non-unitarity, rank-1) and connections to six impossibility theorems from ISO-002 that necessitate external intervention. This matters because it provides a formal framework for grace that rules out Pelagianism and semi-Pelagianism, while highlighting denominational variance on idempotency.
